UF-Ex Docs/Advanced/Optimization.html.title: Preface | UF-Ex Docs
UF-Ex Docs/Advanced/Optimization.html.summary: Preface Suppose you had completed the previous tutorials or already have decent amount of experience in using UF-Ex, you should have quite an amount of code that you had made previously. It is likely that you have developed a mindset "if it works, don't touch it". While this is the safe play, it is not suited for long term development, and we aim to be better than just having the codes work. What is optimization Imagine you are solving a math problem during an exam, you would want to solve it as fast as possible and move on to the next question right? Coding is basically the same, it's best to execute codes as fast as possible so it can run more codes in 1 frame. However, speed isn't everything. Let's say you can bring a cheat sheet to the exam, and of course the fastest way to complete the exam is to have all the answers written on the cheat sheet beforehand. But of course, if there are 100 questions, the cheat sheet will be very messy, if it can even contain all the answers. In coding, the cheat sheet is the Memory stored in RAM. Grabbing data from memory would be fast, but it's not ideal to put a lot of data into memory just so some code can run a bit faster. Optimization in games is to reduce the time for the CPU to process the game's logic, reduce the time for the GPU to render the game's graphics, and to reduce the memory usage in RAM. In other words, make the game less likely to lag. While yes, you may think that because it didn't lag on your computer, then the code is fine. That is not true, it didn't lag on your computer, but there is no guarantee that other people won't experience lag, so it is best to optimize the codes so the chance of lagging reduces. Step 0: Benchmarking So now you understand why should we make codes run faster, but how do we know whether the code did run faster? Of course, you can always use the built-in profiler to check the CPU usage and the Memory Usage, but that's not enough, it is strongly recommended that you install BenchmarkDotNet to your solution so that you can effectively identify what codes need improvement and whether the new ones are improvements at all. Step 1: Important Give concrete examples to optimization using previous tutorial code

UF-Ex Docs/Chart Tutorial/Crash Course.h.title: C# Crash Course | UF-Ex Docs
UF-Ex Docs/Chart Tutorial/Crash Course.h.summary: C# Crash Course Since UF-Ex uses C#, it is expected that you have prior knowledge of C# to use this. If you do not have such knowledge, this section will quickly go over commonly used elements in chart making to jumpstart you with some surface level knowledge. Variables Variables help you store data, you can define a variable like in these formats: <type> <name>; <type> <name> = <value>; <type> <name> = <value>, <name>; <type> <name> = <value>, <name> = <value>; The most commonly used variable types are int (Integers), float (Number with a decimal), char (Single character), string (Text), and bool (Boolean, meaning it's either True or False). For example: int integer = 0; float number = 9.2f; //Note that you need to put "f" at the end of the number to indicate it is a float char character = 'A'; //Single quotation marks for char string text = "Hello World!"; //Double quotation marks for string bool condition_true = true, condition_false = false; int some_number; //This will mark "some_number" as an integer, but it will not have a value assigned to it Operations Code, like Maths, have operation symbols + (Add), - (Subtract), * (Multiply), / (Divide). int a = 5 + 6; //Which is 5 + 6 = 11 int b = a * 6; //Which is 11 * 6 = 66 string text_start = "Hello"; string text_end = " World!"; string full_text = text_start + text_end; //Which is "Hello World!" Keep in mind that sometimes, two different types can be added together, but sometimes it cannot: string something = "Text" + 5; //This will become "Text5" var something_else = 5 + true; //This will result in an error string long_text = "text a" * "text b"; //This will result in an error There are also these operators called compound assignments, it makes operating easier: int a = 5; //Instead of this a = a + 6; //You can do this a += 6; In cases where you want to add or subtract 1, you can use ++ and -- to make it even shorter: int a = 5; a = a + 1; //It becomes 6 a += 1; //It becomes 7 a++; //It becomes 8 a--; //It becomes 7 Collections In some occasions, you might want to store a lot of variables of the same type together, such as: int value_1 = 1; int value_2 = 2; int value_3 = 3; int value_4 = 4; int value_5 = 5; int value_6 = 6; int value_7 = 7; Instead of this, you can use collections like Arrays: int[] values = new int[7]; //This specifies the array to have the length 7 values[0] = 1; //This assigns the first value of the array to be 1 values[1] = 2; //This assigns the second value of the array to be 2 or int[] values = [1, 2, 3, 4, 5, 6, 7]; //Assigns the length of the array and all the values in it You can easily store and retrieve data stored in an array. However, you cannot change the size of an array once you initialized it. If you want a collection where its size can be changed dynamically, you should use a List: List<int> values = [1, 2, 3, 4, 5, 6]; //Assigns the length of the list, type of the list, and the initial values in it values.Add(7); //Adds "7" to the end of the list, increasing its length //The list will become [1, 2, 3, 4, 5, 6, 7] values.RemoveAt(0); //Removes the first element, in this case "1", from the list //The list will become [2, 3, 4, 5, 6, 7] Similiar to arrays, you can read or write values by using values[<index>]. Shorthand initialization Sometimes, the variable name might be longer, such as: EaseUnit<Vector2>[] Eases = new EaseUnit<Vector2>[20]; If you don't want to type the whole variable type out, you can do this instead var Eases = new EaseUnit<Vector2>[20]; It will automatically assign Eases to the defined variable type if it is not ambiguous between multiple variable types. var Eases = new EaseUnit<Vector2>[20]; //Clear definition of EaseUnit<Vector2>[], no issues List<EaseUnit<Vector2>> Eases = []; //Clear definition of List<EastUnit<Vector2>>, no issues EaseUnit<Vector2>[] Eases = []; //Clear definition of EaseUnit<Vector2>[], no issues var Eases = []; //Ambiguous between EaseUnit<Vector2>[], List<EastUnit<Vector2>>, etc., will result in error Statements One of the most important aspects of coding is statements, it's rather straight forward actually. There are some commonly used operators assosiated with it, being == (Equal), != (Not equal), > (Greater than), >= (Greater than or equal), < (Less than), <= (Less than or equal). int a = 5; if (a < 10) //Since a is less than 10, this part will run { //Code } else //Since the part above was already executed, this part will not run { //Code } Similarly int a = 5; if (a > 10) //Since a is not greater than 10, this part will not run { //Code } else //Since the condition above is not true, this part will run { //Code } In some cases, you would like to have a variable that has its value depending on the value of another variable, like: int a = 0, b; if (a == 0) b = 1; else if (a == 1) b = 3; else if (a == 2) b = 9; else b = 12; You may notice that this can quickly become a bit messy, in this case, you can use switch statements: switch (a) { case 0: //When a is 0, execute the following code b = 1; break; //Indicates the code ends here case 1: //When a is 1, execute the following code b = 3; break; //Indicates the code ends here case 2: //When a is 2, execute the following code b = 9; break; //Indicates the code ends here default: //When a is none of the above, execute the following code b = 12; break; //Indicates the code ends here } or b = a switch { 0 => 1, //When a is 0, b is 1 1 => 3, //When a is 1, b is 3 2 => 9, //When a is 2, b is 9 _ => 12 //When a is none of the above, b is 12 }; In some cases, you may run into this type of code: int a = 0, b; if (a == 0) b = 1; else if (a == 1) b = 1; else if (a == 2) b = 9; else b = 12; You can do something like this: switch (a) { case 0: case 1: b = 1; //When a is 1 or 0, execute this break; case 2: //Same as before b = 9; break; default: b = 12; break; } //Or this b = a switch { 0 or 1 => 3, //When a is 0 or 1, b is 3 2 => 9, //When a is 2, b is 9 _ => 12 //When a is none of the above, b is 12 }; Functions Functions help you perform repetitive tasks, you can define a function like this: <return_type> <name>(<type> <name>, <type> <name>, ...) { //Code return Some_value; //If necessary } For example instead of the following: ///csharp int a = 5, b = 6; float c = (a + b) / 2f; You can do this instead: ```csharp float Mean(int value_a, int value_b) { return (value_a + value_b) / 2f; } int a = 5, b = 6; float c = Mean(a, b); If the function only contains one line of code, like the one above, you can use an expression called lambda expression instead: float Mean(int value_a, int value_b) => (value_a + value_b) / 2f; Of course, you can define a function that does not return anything: void SomeFunction() { //Code //In this case, you do not need to add "return" as there is nothing to return } This also means that you cannot do something like this: float c = SomeFunction(); Loops Let's say you have an array: int[] values = [1, 2, 3, 4, 5, 6, 7]; And you want all the values to increase by 1, so that it will become [2, 3, 4, 5, 6, 7, 8], while you can manually add them like this: values[0]++; values[1]++; values[2]++; values[3]++; values[4]++; values[5]++; values[6]++; values[7]++; You'd probably wonder if there are any better ways to handle this, and there are! They are loops, one of them are while loops, you can use them like this: //Defines i as 0 int i = 0; //Checks whether i is less than the length of the array, if so, run the code while (i < value.Length) { //Increases the i-th index of the array by 1 values[i]++; //Increases i by 1 i++; //Goes back to the check } //The loop ended However, in cases like these, there is an even better loop for it, it's called for loops: for (<type> <name> = <value>; <condition>; <action>) { //Code } For the above example, the example code would be this: for (int i = 0; i < values.Length; i++) { values[i]++; } You may notice that it is functionally the same as the above while loop. Using statement In UF-Ex, you are likely to use other namespaces or types to use their functions, for example: float radian = UndyneFight_Ex.MathUtil.GetRadian(100); ICustomMotion motion = UndyneFight_Ex.Entities.Motions.RotationRoute.linear; As you may see, it's tedious to type out "UndyneFight_Ex.XXX" every single time we have to reference it, so you can use using to simplify the process, the syntax is as follows: using (namespace name); using the_above_example; (Please laugh) using UndyneFight_Ex; float radian = MathUtil.GetRadian(100); ICustomMotion motion = Entities.Motions.RotationRoute.linear; Sometimes, you would want to simplify static types that are highlighted in green (in default), such as MathUtil. To simplify these static members, you can simply use using static UndyneFight_Ex.MathUtil; float radian = GetRadian(100); Note that this does not imply UndyneFight_Ex will be used, so you still need to type out using UndyneFight_Ex;. Conclusion In this chapter, you have: Understood how variables are defined and used. How to operate on variables. Using branching conditionals if, else, and switch. Creating and using functions. How a For loop and a While loop works. Utilizing namespaces and static classes. Tip You can always search online for more information about C# to make coding easier, just make sure the codes don't get too messy ^o^/.

UF-Ex Docs/Chart Tutorial/Making.html.title: Charting with UF-Ex | UF-Ex Docs
UF-Ex Docs/Chart Tutorial/Making.html.summary: Charting with UF-Ex This tutorial will go over fundemental concepts you will utilize in creating charts with UF-Ex, we will create two charts that act as an interactive example for various concepts you will learn throughout this and future tutorials. When completed, the finished products can equip you with the nessecary knowledge and tools to jumpstart the development of future charts should you like to create more. While the worked examples are provided in the repository, it is strongly encouraged that you create your own file and type in the codes yourself to familarize yourself with the development flow. What we will chart Important Actually decide what to chart Target readers It is best if you have fundemental C# knowledge so you will be more comfortable with Object-Oriented-Programming (OOP). If you do not have prior C# knowledge, you can either visit the official Microsoft tutorial or read the crash course Note from author Hi, I'm TK, I had been a Rhythm Recall player since some time around 2022 and was invited into the development team later the same year. Contrary to public belief, this is how I first learnt about C#, I never knew anything about it beforehand aside from GML. For the first few months, I focused on implementing quality of life (QoL) updates to UF-Ex from my experience as a player. While I was just starting off in C#, I noticed that the organization and optimization of UF-Ex was horrible, it didn't even have actual tutorials except for a few .pdf files from Tlott that was of little help, and the structure of UF-Ex was nowhere near the tutorial from MonoGame. Eventually T-mas, the original creator, abandoned the project and moved over to develop Undyne Fight Role Play Game (UFRPG), and due to the overwhelmingly negative receptions, he open sourced the entire source code of Rhythm Recall without asking any other members. My feelings aside, that provided me motivation to improve UF-Ex as a whole by cutting down reduntant codes and speed up the development cycle using my position in the community. After two years of hard work on maintaining UF-Ex, I decided that it can be open sourced since the codes are now somewhat presentable, though still hard to pick up due to the lack of documentation. I understand that charting using UF-Ex can be difficult at first, considering I had been there before, so I hope to teach other people how to use UF-Ex to its full extent with this documentation, and that people won't spend far too much time on things that can be easily done. I hope that from this documentation, you can learn more about UF-Ex and I can learn more about maintaining a project. Happy coding! TK (I am very tired.)

UF-Ex Docs/Chart Tutorial/Setting Up.htm.title: Setting Up | UF-Ex Docs
UF-Ex Docs/Chart Tutorial/Setting Up.htm.summary: Setting Up Installing MSVS + UF-Ex Notes You can either use Visual Studio Code or Visual Studio to use this engine, however this tutorial only covers Visual Studio, if you intend to use Visual Studio Code, you might need to figure some aspects out yourself. The documentation may be updated over time, if you are using the PDF version of it, remember to check the site occasionally for the latest changes. Requirements Microsoft Visual Studio (MSVS) Visual C++ Redistributable Packages for Visual Studio 2013 (Install this first) .NET 9.0 (C# 13 or higher) UF-Ex project files (Included in the example solution) 8 GB of disk space, 4 GB of RAM The courage to ask for help. Installing Visual Studio Visual Studio Community is sufficient for this engine, you don’t have to install Professional or Enterprise. You have to install .NET desktop development and WinUI application development in order for the UF-Ex engine to function. VS extension development is optional. Setting up the solution After installing MSVS, open the provided example solution, you can name it whatever you like. Open the solution (.sln), select “Extensions” at the top bar, and then choose “Manage Extensions” Choose it and search for “Monogame” Install the extension shown in the image. (Note that the extension version in the image is outdated, ensure you have the latest version installed) After installing Monogame Framework, search for “HLSL” Install the extension shown in the image. (You can choose to not install this if you can read HLSL shader codes in pure text.) Note that you may need to restart your computer/MSVS after installing certain components. After finishing the installation process, open MSVS and go to the solution explorer on the right hand side, Right click “Dependencies” and select “Add project reference” Click “Browse” and select UndyneFight_Ex.dll. Updating UF-Ex Since the example solution already has the latest version of the UF-Ex project included, the SDK will automatically be updated along with the repository, therefore you only need to delete the original reference folder and replace it with the new one. Importing music By pressing (Ctrl +) F5, the game should run normally (And then you will see a hideous UI). (Ctrl + F5 will not attach the debugger to the executable, it will run faster but will not show an error log when the game crashes.) If you try to select a song, you should see this. A bracket indicates that there is no associated music file for the chart, that means you need to import it. To import assets, select “Content.mgcb” in the “Content” folder You can just double click it or choose “Open With -> MGCB Editor”. If there is no such folder named “Musics”, create one by right clicking “Content”, and select “Add -> New Folder” and name it “Musics”. After having the “Musics” folder, create a folder that matches the name of the chart, in this case, it would be “My First Chart”. Right click on the newly created folder and select “Add -> Existing Item”, then you can select the music you want to import, make sure it says the imported music is set to a song. After importing the music, rename the music asset into “song.(file type)” (If the music you imported was an .wav file, name it to song.wav, and so on) If you want to add a chart cover, simply import an image file and rename it into “paint.png”. Note: The engine has auto scaling for chart covers, but it is best to set it to a 4:3 ratio to avoid visual bugs. After importing the chart assets, make sure to “Build” the MGCB by pressing F6. Tip It is best to use “Rebuild” if you have removed or renamed assets. Basic template information Some comments are inside “Normal Model” and “Championship Model”, you may view them for further information. IWaveSet (Classic) IWaveSetS (Simplified) class MyFirstChart : WaveConstructor, IWaveSet WaveConstructor contains the basic methods for charting such as beat calculation and the main chart making function. IWaveSet is the interface that stores the basic information of the chart, such as the difficulties and music name. public MyFirstChart() : base(62.5f / (100 / 60f)) { } The “100” is the BPM of the chart, if you are unsure of the BPM, you can use an online BPM checker or use Malody (More accurate) to find the BPM of the music. If there are multiple BPM in the chart, simply put them in arrays like this: public MyFirstChart() : base([10, 300], [10, 50], [999, 230]) { } This means that the first 10 beats have 300 bpm, the next 10 beats have 50 bpm, and the next 999 beats have 230 bpm. Most information are already provided in "Normal Model.cs", you may view the basic setup there. Sometimes, you may find that you need to copy and paste chunks of code from one difficulty to another, and when you need to change certain aspects of the code, you need to manually change them all. Not only is this process boring and tedious, it makes the code unreadable and too large. In short, this is poor coding practice and should be avoided. To simplify the charting process, IWaveSetS is created, your code can now look as simple as this public void Chart() { Effect(); switch (CurrentDifficulty) { case Difficulty.Noob: //Noob mode break; case Difficulty.Normal: //Normal mode break; } } Or even this public void Chart() { if (InBeat(0)) { int spd = CurrentDifficulty switch { Difficulty.Noob => 4, Difficulty.Easy => 5, Difficulty.Normal => 6 } CreateChart(0, BeatTime(1), spd, ["R", "", "", "etc"]); } } Not only is the code more efficient, it is more readable and easy to keep track of. Conclusion In this chapter, you have: Set up your computer to develop on UF-Ex. Installed the required dependencies such as MonoGame. Created an empty folder for My First Chart. In the next chapter, we will start creating the chart.

UF-Ex Docs/api/Extends.Someway.html.summary: Class Someway Namespace Extends Assembly UndyneFight-Ex.dll [Obsolete("There are better functions")] public static class Someway Inheritance object Someway Inherited Members object.GetType() object.MemberwiseClone() object.ToString() object.Equals(object) object.Equals(object, object) object.ReferenceEquals(object, object) object.GetHashCode() Methods SpecialRhythmCreate(float, float, float, string[], string[], Action[]) 使用一个特殊的节奏数组,并且支持在定点释放事件。 规则如下： eventsname和events是对应的。例如第二个eventsname对应第二个events。 GB的创建即 "G001"，G表示固定方向，第二个字符为方向，第三个字符为颜色，第三个之后的字符表示持续beat拍（默认-5） "WR01"，W表示随机方向，第二个字符没有效果，第三个字符为颜色，第三个之后的字符表示持续beat拍（默认-5） "/"为空拍,x表示切分拍 箭头第一个字符-方向 的规则: R 表示随机 D 表示与上次不同 +x 表示上一个方向的 +x方向 -x 表示上一个方向的 -x方向 $x 表示固定某个方向。 箭头第二个字符-颜色 的规则：0蓝1红。 箭头第三个字符-旋转type 的规则：0普通1旋转2斜矛。 箭头修饰字符-箭头效果 的规则：前面加上~表示*1.2速加速，!表示右旋转，@表示左旋转 箭头组合规则：字符串内加括号表示不仅创建一个箭头,例如"(R)(R1)"。 PS："R(+0)" ≠ "(R)(+0)",后者才是两个矛叠一块，第一个会无效。 [Obsolete("Use CreateChart()")] public static void SpecialRhythmCreate(float beat, float arrowspeed, float starttime, string[] rhythm, string[] eventsname, Action[] events) Parameters beat float 节奏数组的间隔拍，推荐三十二分音符为间隔 arrowspeed float 假如创建出来箭头，那么这个箭头的速度 starttime float 延迟的时间 rhythm string[] 节奏数组 eventsname string[] 节奏数组内事件的名称 events Action[] 节奏数组内的事件

Optional Args: "!": No Score, "^": Accelerate, "<": RotateL, ">": RotateR, "": Tap, "~": Void Sprite, "_": Hold Order of parsing: ~_<>^! Direction Args: "R": Random, "D": Different, "+/-x" Add/Sub x to the last dir. , "$x": Fixed on x direction, "Nx": Not x, "Ax": The xth allocated direction Optional Color Args: 0-> Blue, 1-> Red, 2-> Green, 3-> Purple Optional Rotation Args: 0-> None, 1-> Reverse, 2-> Diagonal GB：#xx#yz, Where "xx" means the duration beat, "y" beats direction, "z" means color, replace '#' with '%' if you don't want arrows Combinations: "(R)(+0)", NOT "R(+0)" Misc: use ' to multiply the speed of the arrow, << or >> to adjust the current beat (>>0.5 will skip 0.5 beats) Use RegisterFunction(string, Action) or RegisterFunctionOnce(string, Action) to declare functions to execute them inside here For example RegisterFunctionOnce("func", ()=> {}); "(func)(R)", will invoke the action in "func" and creates an arrow "!!X/Y", Each item will last 'Beat / 2X' beats (i.e. X = 2 then 1 beat is 4 items instead of the usual 8) for the next Y beats (If Y is undefined then it will last for the rest of the function) You can add arguments in the form of "<Arg1,Arg2...>Action" You may use Arguments inside the declared action in RegisterFunction(Once) to access them. UF-Ex Docs/introduction.html.title: Welcome | UF-Ex Docs
UF-Ex Docs/introduction.html.summary: Welcome Welcome to the introduction section of the UF-Ex documentation, here you can find tutorials and frequently asked questions on how to use the UF-Ex SDK. UndyneFight-Ex, or UF-Ex for short, is a .NET SDK used to create Undertale themed rhythm games for desktop PCs using the language C#, with the implementation of MonoGame Framework, MonoGame Extended, NAudio, Newtonsoft, and NVorbis. The SDK was used to create Rhythm Recall, and now Rhythm Recall Rcade. This SDK is the continuation of the incomplete version of the SDK which was open sourced along with the incomplete Rhythm Recall v0.2.2 in here. This SDK provides additional features such as: Localization Additional utilities for development Audio preview for charts Rebinding keys Multiple BPM in charts User defined easing functions Typo correction in codes Documentation of codes Optimization to codes And more This documentation aims to help you get started with developing using this SDK with a step by step guide from setting up to publishing your game. Send help if you would like to assist in the development of the SDK in any way, you can go to the Github page or Discord server to provide your assistance! Code This open sourced (since 2025) project is maintained by only one person and a few bug testers, it would be great if you can help by reporting bugs, make a feature request, or even create a pull request to help development gain momentum. Documentation As mentioned above, this project is maintained by one person only, so the production speed of the documentation would be slow, if you have a good understanding on how UF-Ex works, you can help by creating guides, videos, or improvements to the documentation to further help other people understand how to use this SDK. Cross platform UF-Ex is (currently) a Windows only SDK, and that is obviously not very friendly to people who aren't using Windows. If you have a non-Windows machine and knows coding, you can help by testing whether this SDK can run smoothly on different machines.

api/Extends.Someway.html.summary: Class Someway Namespace Extends Assembly UndyneFight-Ex.dll [Obsolete("There are better functions")] public static class Someway Inheritance object Someway Inherited Members object.Equals(object) object.Equals(object, object) object.GetHashCode() object.GetType() object.MemberwiseClone() object.ReferenceEquals(object, object) object.ToString() Methods SpecialRhythmCreate(float, float, float, string[], string[], Action[]) 使用一个特殊的节奏数组,并且支持在定点释放事件。 规则如下： eventsname和events是对应的。例如第二个eventsname对应第二个events。 GB的创建即 "G001"，G表示固定方向，第二个字符为方向，第三个字符为颜色，第三个之后的字符表示持续beat拍（默认-5） "WR01"，W表示随机方向，第二个字符没有效果，第三个字符为颜色，第三个之后的字符表示持续beat拍（默认-5） "/"为空拍,x表示切分拍 箭头第一个字符-方向 的规则: R 表示随机 D 表示与上次不同 +x 表示上一个方向的 +x方向 -x 表示上一个方向的 -x方向 $x 表示固定某个方向。 箭头第二个字符-颜色 的规则：0蓝1红。 箭头第三个字符-旋转type 的规则：0普通1旋转2斜矛。 箭头修饰字符-箭头效果 的规则：前面加上~表示*1.2速加速，!表示右旋转，@表示左旋转 箭头组合规则：字符串内加括号表示不仅创建一个箭头,例如"(R)(R1)"。 PS："R(+0)" ≠ "(R)(+0)",后者才是两个矛叠一块，第一个会无效。 [Obsolete("Use CreateChart()")] public static void SpecialRhythmCreate(float beat, float arrowspeed, float starttime, string[] rhythm, string[] eventsname, Action[] events) Parameters beat float 节奏数组的间隔拍，推荐三十二分音符为间隔 arrowspeed float 假如创建出来箭头，那么这个箭头的速度 starttime float 延迟的时间 rhythm string[] 节奏数组 eventsname string[] 节奏数组内事件的名称 events Action[] 节奏数组内的事件
